correctness.rationale: Reconstructed all six matrix coefficients in N4 over arbitrary finite field k, direct products XY−YX and exactly three independent constraints: aD−dA, dF−fD, aE+bF−eA−fB; c and C are central/free. Equality of commutants is equivalent to equality of rowspaces in k^5 for the displayed three-row matrix. Four exhaustive cases on d and (a,f) produce ranks/fiber pairs: (0,1), (1,q−1) with q+1 projective lines; rank 2 with q³+q² generic kernels each effective fiber q−1, plus one exceptional kernel with effective fiber q²(q−1); rank 3 with q³−q distinct parameters (alpha=a/d,phi=f/d,gamma=(phi b−alpha e)/d), each effective fiber q(q−1). In the rank-three case the intersection with A,D,F intrinsic subspace determines alpha,phi, and the normalized remaining row determines gamma, proving injectivity; every triple is attained. Multiplying each effective fiber by free c multiplies by q, yielding theorem table. The codimension count sum is 2q³+q²+3, and weighted fiber sum is q^6; group relation follows from the 1+X algebra group multiplication identity for all characteristics, including 2. Independent direct kernel (not RREF) enumeration over F2,F3,F4,F5 builds every element’s actual commuting set by checking all candidate Y in 5 effective coordinates, then groups by identical kernel sets. It verifies every centralizer count and every fiber multiplicity: total 23,66,147,278 respectively; extension F4 handled by irreducible t²+t+1. These are finite checks; arbitrary-q conclusion follows only from the four-case proof. No unproved infinite extrapolation from computation.

originality.rationale: The complete equality quotient of the centralizer map is not stated or established by the inspected earlier papers or relevant prior published mathematical results. The 2015 Kumar–Prajapati paper explicitly defines equality of group centralizers, proves rank-three regular subsets and q²(q−1) classes (with q(q−1)-element fibers) in N2, so those parts are not new. Its Theorem 15 and N2 Lemma 22 do not, alone, compute all centralizer equality classes, notably the q+1 rank-one kernels, the exceptional rank-two kernel with q³(q−1) fiber, the combined q³+q² generic rank-two kernels, or the rank-three union and whole-group fiber partition. Kaur–Sharma–Singh 2020 Table/Thm 6.1 classifies conjugacy / isomorphism types and commuting tuple branching, not equality of actual embedded centralizers; rank marginals and zero commutator fibers in the October 12 published N4 result similarly lack subspace equivalence information. Majeed–Ramkumar 2026 is especially plausible same-object primary work, but full text could not be accessed in this execution (arXiv and OA PDF failed; Oxford VPN disconnected). Its abstract covers commuting graph and clique structure, not an explicit complete embedded centralizer quotient; cannot conclude it lacks such a theorem based on the abstract. Thus PASS is qualified best-of-knowledge, not proof of publication priority.
